question: What is the primary function of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: To treat individual patients in acute care settings
options.B: The systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data
options.C: To enforce strict quarantine laws without data collection
options.D: To manufacture vaccines during an epidemic

explanation: Disease surveillance is defined as the systematic, ongoing collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data essential for planning and public health action. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is disease surveillance considered an early warning system for nursing professionals?

options.A: It predicts the exact weather patterns causing disease
options.B: It helps detect unusual patterns of illness and monitors trends over time
options.C: It automatically cures patients before they arrive at the hospital
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory testing in rural clinics

explanation: Surveillance acts as an early warning system by continuously monitoring health status to detect unusual illness patterns and health trends. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: What is a major objective of public health surveillance in Nigeria?

options.A: To generate revenue for local government clinics
options.B: To track the natural history of diseases and detect epidemics
options.D: To prescribe medications without a physician's oversight

explanation: Tracking the natural history of diseases and detecting epidemics are core objectives of public health surveillance. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: How does tracking meningitis cases prior to the dry season help health authorities?

options.A: It allows them to preposition vaccines and antibiotics
options.B: It stops the dry season from occurring
options.C: It completely eliminates the bacterium from the environment
options.D: It reduces the need for community education

explanation: Tracking seasonal trends allows health authorities to preposition necessary medical supplies like vaccines and antibiotics before an outbreak peaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: Which type of surveillance relies on healthcare providers submitting reports voluntarily or through standard protocols without active prompting?
explanation: Passive surveillance relies on healthcare providers initiating reports through routine protocols, though it is prone to underreporting. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the primary characteristic of syndromic surveillance?

options.A: It waits for definitive laboratory confirmation before recording any data
options.B: It tracks clinical features and symptoms before lab diagnosis is confirmed
options.C: It is only conducted once every ten years during a census
options.D: It exclusively monitors non-communicable chronic illnesses

explanation: Syndromic surveillance focuses on clinical signs and symptoms to enable the earliest possible detection of potential outbreaks before lab confirmation. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the very first stage in the core disease surveillance cycle described in the text?
explanation: The surveillance cycle begins with data generation and collection by frontline healthcare workers and institutions. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why is feedback and dissemination important in the surveillance process?

options.A: To punish clinics that fail to report cases
options.B: To share findings back with reporting sites and policymakers to guide practice
options.C: To replace the need for data analysis
options.D: To increase the cost of healthcare delivery

explanation: Feedback and dissemination ensure that findings are shared with reporting sites and policymakers to maintain awareness and guide clinical decisions. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: What is the primary standardized framework used for disease surveillance across Nigerian health facilities?
explanation: The IDSR strategy is the primary framework used to standardize disease data gathering across health facilities in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is the purpose of electronic systems like SORMAS in Nigerian public health?

options.A: To replace doctors in diagnosing complex surgeries
options.B: To improve real-time data collection and reduce reporting delays during outbreaks
options.D: To manage patient financial billing in private hospitals

explanation: SORMAS and similar electronic tools are used to enhance real-time data collection and minimize reporting delays during disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is the first operational priority when an unusual spike in disease incidence is flagged by surveillance?

options.B: Mobilizing a multidisciplinary rapid response team to investigate
options.D: Waiting three months to see if the disease resolves on its own

explanation: An unusual spike triggers the mobilization of a rapid response team to verify the diagnosis and investigate the potential outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Which of the following describes a key nursing responsibility during a disease outbreak response?

options.A: Enforcing strict infection prevention and control (IPC) protocols and managing isolation
options.B: Performing epidemiological research trials independently abroad
options.C: Manufacturing commercial vaccines in hospital wards

explanation: Nurses play a critical role during outbreaks by maintaining IPC standards, managing isolation wards, and providing direct patient care. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned for frontline disease surveillance?

options.A: They control the national health budget allocation
options.B: They interact daily with patients and families, allowing them to notice unusual health trends early
options.C: They are the only healthcare professionals permitted to use laboratory microscopes
options.D: They spend most of their time in administrative offices away from patients

explanation: Nurses have daily contact with patients and communities, placing them in an ideal position to detect anomalous health trends first. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: What is an important community-level action nurses perform to support disease surveillance?

options.A: Conducting contact tracing and educating the public on early warning signs
options.B: Imposing fines on households with sick individuals
options.C: Isolating entire towns without notifying health ministries
options.D: Destroying all local clinic registers annually

explanation: Nurses support surveillance by conducting contact tracing, educating the public, and encouraging early healthcare-seeking behaviors. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: What is a major operational challenge facing disease surveillance systems in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of fully trained epidemiologists in every rural clinic
options.B: Underreporting, personnel shortages, and infrastructural deficits
options.C: Too many digital reporting tools causing system overload
options.D: The complete absence of infectious diseases in the country

explanation: Surveillance is frequently hindered by underreporting, shortages of trained staff, and infrastructural deficits such as poor internet and power supply. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)

question: How can future public health strategies help overcome current surveillance barriers?

options.A: By stopping all community engagement activities
options.B: By scaling up digital health technologies and training healthcare workers
options.C: By removing all reporting forms and relying solely on guesswork
options.D: By isolating primary healthcare centers from national networks

explanation: Scaling up digital health technologies and continuously training healthcare workers are key future directions for strengthening surveillance. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)
